page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4g.32xlarge is a local SSD storage-focused instance designed around large-scale processing and direct-attached storage requirements. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by a KVM hypervisor, it features 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 512.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 ratio with 4.0 GB per core.

A prominent characteristic of this instance configuration is its 7679 GB of integrated local SSD storage, which eliminates reliance on network-attached block devices for high-throughput disk access. Complementing the internal storage array is a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, facilitating substantial throughput across distributed topologies. No graphics hardware accelerators are present on this platform.

The hardware configuration delivers high compute and memory density within a single node. Bundling 7679 GB of local SSD avoids external storage egress and provisioning overheads, making it resource-efficient for large working datasets. However, local storage architectures typically lack the automated durability guarantees of persistent network-attached block volumes, requiring external replication or backup mechanisms.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4g.32xlarge is suitable for storage-intensive and I/O-heavy enterprise operations, including distributed databases, NoSQL engines, large-scale search indices, real-time analytics, and data-intensive ETL processing pipelines that require substantial local capacity and consistent multi-threaded compute.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i4g.32xlarge is a storage-optimized instance tailored for high-capacity I/O operations and dense parallel compute. Governed by a KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 platform, the server is equipped with 128 dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz and 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include 7679 GB of integrated local SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 64 Gbps, while omitting GPU hardware accelerators. Integrating vast local disk arrays directly with substantial dedicated compute reduces network latency for disk operations, though workloads must account for the ephemeral characteristics of local disk architectures. Given its extensive capacity and 64 Gbps network layer, the instance is well matched for high-throughput distributed databases, large-scale NoSQL deployments, elastic search indexing, data warehousing, and demanding analytical ETL processing pipelines requiring substantial local disk space.
